clue.text: Visionary vacuum cleaner perhaps puckered fabric

parts.note: a visionary is a seer, one who sees the future
a vacuum cleaner is one example of a sucker, something that sucks

explanation.surface: A prophetic vacuum cleaner seems to be wrinkling up some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a thin cotton cloth woven with a crinkled, puckered stripe.

clue.text: Blubber keeping lake's chill out

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the lake letter sits within the crying word

parts.note: to blubber is to sob noisily
L is the abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: A tearful outburst holding back the lake's cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' is a verb here, not whale fat.
explanation.definitionFit: To slob, or slob about, is to laze idly, to relax lazily.

clue.text: After hesitation, married couple maybe taking ages outside fabulous land

indicators.note: after puts the hesitation sound in front, leading the answer

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

indicators.note: taking the married pair in means the ages word holds them
outside says the ages word goes round the couple's letters

parts.note: an eon is an age, an immensely long time
W and H stand for wife and husband, one example of a married couple

explanation.surface: After some dithering, a wedded pair spend years far from a mythical country.
explanation.definitionFit: Erewhon is the imaginary country of Samuel Butler's satirical novel, its name nowhere backwards.

clue.text: Clothing accessory digs into joints

definitions.note: the singular 'accessory' stands for the pair of pads as one item

indicators.note: going into another word means sitting inside it

parts.note: shoulders are joints of the body
digs and pad are both slang for lodgings, a place to live

explanation.surface: A garment add-on that pokes into the body's joints.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoulder pads are padding sewn into jackets to broaden the shoulders, famously in the 1980s.

clue.text: Pictures shown here of pencil doodling echo times

indicators.note: doodling is aimless scribbling, so the letters of pencil wander into a new order

parts.note: Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Pictures of pencil scribbles repeated several times, on show here.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineplex is a multi-screen cinema, a place where films, the pictures, are shown.

clue.text: Make mistakes penning answer, periodically applying this?

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so the picked letters go inside

parts.note: to err is to make mistakes

indicators.note: periodically picks letters at regular intervals, here the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Getting an answer wrong, you turn to this every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: after making mistakes you apply a rubber, so this is what is applied.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser is a rubber, the tool rubbed on a page to remove pencil errors.

clue.text: Barman's mass of ice

definitions.meaning: a 'barman' here is a man of musical bars; the 's stands for 'is'
a floating mass of ice, short for iceberg

explanation.surface: A bartender is apparently a lump of ice: cold service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' is not a pub worker but a writer of musical bars: Alban Berg, the Austrian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Berg is the short form of iceberg, a large floating block broken from a glacier.

clue.text: Turkish official that is upset about very loud curtains

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the overturned pair of letters goes round the rest
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is (id est)
FF is fortissimo in music, very loud
curtains means the end, as in 'it's curtains for him'

explanation.surface: A Turkish dignitary, unsettled by noisy drapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the abbreviation backwards to EI before 'about' wraps it round the rest; 'curtains' is slang for the end, not drapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi was a title of respect for a man of standing or official rank in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Penguin territory acquired food given by Sydney, say

parts.note: got means acquired, obtained
ham is a meat, a food
Sydney is one example of a city

explanation.surface: A patch of penguin habitat gained, with food given by an Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: The Penguin is not a bird but Batman's villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Gotham City is Batman's home, where the villain called the Penguin operates.

clue.text: A free agent on broadcast probing drawback of celebrity

indicators.note: something probing goes into another piece, so the scattered-seed word sits within the fame word
drawn back means read from the end to the start, so the fame word runs backwards

parts.note: celebrity or fame is having a name
broadcast seed is sown, scattered by hand

explanation.surface: An independent pundit on the airwaves digs into the downside of fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback of' reverses the fame word to EMAN, and 'probing' splits it E...MAN around the sowing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is their own man answers to nobody, a free agent acting independently.

clue.text: Removing odd bits of leaf lifts impression of fence?

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves the second, fourth, sixth and eighth of the two words

explanation.surface: Plucking at a leaf lifts the print of a garden fence.
explanation.walkthrough: The fence is the criminal kind, a receiver of stolen goods, so this is a police likeness of one.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-fit is a computer-built likeness of a suspect, and a fence is a criminal dealer in stolen goods.

clue.text: Elusive rogue dealer, half-hidden, nobody rumbled

parts.note: an imp is a little rogue, a mischievous rascal

indicators.note: rumbled means found out and disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order
with half of it hidden only the first half of nobody is used

explanation.surface: A slippery crooked trader, half out of sight, was found out by no one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hidden' leaves NOB from nobody, and 'rumbled' mixes it with DEALER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imponderable cannot be weighed or assessed, so it slips from one's grasp.

clue.text: Welshman tailed driver without licence — here?

definitions.text: Welshman tailed driver without licence — here?

indicators.note: a tailed word has had its tail, the final letter, docked like a lamb's

parts.note: Rhys is a common Welsh man's name
L is the plate shown by a learner, a driver who holds no full licence yet, which 'without licence' spells out

explanation.surface: A Welsh motorist was followed while driving unlicensed; the question is where.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a Welsh resort is just where a Welshman might trail a learner. Rhyl is a seaside town on the north Wales coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyl, a town in north Wales, is a fitting scene for a Welsh driver, hence the query about location.

clue.text: Geordie wrestler cutting head, in pain, developed illness

indicators.note: the Geordie and wrestler pieces are placed in the rearranged pain letters
developed means worked into a new form, so the letters of pain are rearranged

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

indicators.note: cutting the head removes the first letter of the wrestler word

parts.note: a sumo is a Japanese wrestler

explanation.surface: A Newcastle grappler, butting heads in agony, falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting head' drops the wrestler's first letter; 'developed' rearranges pain as PNIA, and 'in' puts the North East and wrestler pieces after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pneumonia is a lung infection, a serious illness.

clue.text: Make progress in freezing conditions pulling up ocean's fish

indicators.note: pulling up in a down clue means drawn upwards, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: the deep is the ocean; the 's gives the plural-looking deeps
a skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Getting ahead in icy weather by hauling up sea creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed-skate is to race on ice skates, moving fast across a frozen surface.

clue.text: Golf aim disheartened Clive, thinking seriously about specs

parts.note: a golfer aims for the pin, the flagstick in the hole

indicators.note: with its heart gone only the first and last letters of the name remain
about here means turned round, so the meditation word is read backwards

parts.note: Zen is a school of meditation, deep and serious thought

explanation.surface: Clive, gloomy about his golf, ponders whether glasses would help.
explanation.definitionFit: Pince-nez are old-fashioned spectacles clipped to the nose without side arms.

clue.text: Unknown roused a disco, removing small sparkly belt

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, here Z

indicators.note: roused means stirred up, so the letters are mixed
removing takes the small letter out of the stirred-up letters

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: A stranger livens up a nightclub, taking off a little glittery belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roused' shuffles A DISCO and 'removing' drops S, leaving ODIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac is the band of sky through which the sun and planets move, studded with constellations.

clue.text: Saucy dressing to catch the eye in pub outlet and club abroad

indicators.note: to catch means to hold inside, so the sauce word wraps round the rest

parts.note: jus is a thin meat sauce served as a dressing
a vent is an outlet for air or steam

indicators.note: the eye of something is its centre, so this picks the middle letter

explanation.surface: A cheeky outfit to attract attention at the pub's outlet, and at a club overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Juventus is a major Italian football club based in Turin.

clue.text: Electronics accessed by crack motor-racing team?

indicators.note: being accessed by something means it gets inside, so the joke word goes within

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, and the plural gives two of them
a crack is a wisecrack, a quip

explanation.surface: A motor-racing outfit hacked into for its electronics, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipe is a French word for team, borrowed for racing teams in motorsport.

clue.text: In the dark, a conflict is dominated by an Alsatian

indicators.note: being dominated by something means being held within its control, so the war goes inside

parts.note: une is French for an; Alsace is a French-speaking region
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: Unseen in the darkness, a fight is won by a German shepherd dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alsatian' looks like the dog breed but means someone from Alsace, a French speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark is to be ignorant of something, uninformed.

clue.text: Fashion designer keeps a drawer for measuring device

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it inside

parts.note: Mary Quant was the British fashion designer famous for the miniskirt
Dr is the abbreviation for drawer, the person who writes a cheque

explanation.surface: A couturier holds onto a chest of drawers in which to keep a tape measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrant is an old instrument for measuring angles and altitudes, as in navigation.

clue.text: A series of bike races involving fields in any event

indicators.note: involving means including, so the meadows go inside

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the motorcycle race series on the Isle of Man
leas are meadows, fields

explanation.surface: A motorcycle championship that runs through open fields, whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: At least is an idiom meaning anyway, in any case.

clue.text: Team rowing hard, last in quarter-final?

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A crew labouring heavily, bottom of a knockout tie.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarter-final stage has eight competitors, so the one that comes last is the eighth.
explanation.definitionFit: With eight entrants left at the quarter-final stage, the bottom placing is the eighth.

clue.text: Stomach discharge to remain constant

parts.note: to stomach something is to stand it, to tolerate it
to fire a gun is to discharge it

explanation.surface: Instructions for dealing with digestive trouble, keeping things steady.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand fire is to keep one's position under enemy shooting, staying steadfast and unmoved.

clue.text: Bank on lavatory being vacant

definitions.note: to bank, used with the following 'on', means to depend; the answer stands for the verb alone

parts.note: re means on or about, as in business letters

indicators.note: a vacant word is emptied of its inside letters, keeping only its ends

explanation.surface: Counting on the toilet being free.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to depend on them, to bank on them.

clue.text: PM's need for reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges the cabinet, so these letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: A prime minister needs a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was British prime minister from 1955 to 1957.

clue.text: Legendary warrior's degenerate weapon mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word for growing old is given by its sound only

parts.note: to degenerate is to age, to decline with time
ax is the American spelling of axe, a weapon

explanation.surface: A mythical fighter's weapon has, it is said, gone to pot.
explanation.walkthrough: AJ is written for the sound of AGE; 'mentioned' covers only that piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was a Greek hero of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad, a mighty warrior.

clue.text: Little piece by hack accepted by editor for Oldie

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit'

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken inside it

parts.note: to hack something is to bear it, as in 'can't hack it'

explanation.surface: A short article from a journalist taken on by the editor of The Oldie magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oldie is a British magazine for older readers, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitebeard is an old man, one whose beard has turned white with age.

clue.text: One serves drinks right after lamb?

indicators.note: after places the right letter following the sheep word

parts.note: a ewe lamb is a female lamb, so a lamb may be a ewe

explanation.surface: Someone pours out drinks, properly, after the lamb course.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug, a vessel from which water or wine is poured.

clue.text: Writer's item for storing college files foremost in room

parts.note: a chest is a box for storing things

indicators.note: to file in is to walk in one after another, so the room letter goes into the college

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school, Eton College

indicators.note: foremost in picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An author's storage cabinet where his papers come first in the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foremost in' gives R, which 'files' sends into ETON.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was the English writer of the Father Brown detective stories.
